% ========================================================================
% DG6: HOW LARGE A DIFFERENCE THE AGENT-LAYER COMPARISON COULD SEE
% SINGLE+G against MULTI-G on the same items at the loose budget
% (analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.csv). Margins are declared as a fraction of
% an effect this study already measured on the same items: the effect of
% adding the guard at a fixed architecture. Margins in percentage points
% and detectable risk differences carry no per-cent sign, and business
% hours are unitless, as everywhere else in this file. Intervals,
% equivalence verdicts and design power for the agent-layer comparison,
% from the regenerated guard-v0.2 artifact. The pass-through outcome
% applies the V4/V6 content rule (code/scripts/passthrough_rule.py); false
% block and catch are dispositions and are unchanged.
% ========================================================================
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.md 'End-task quality: primary' margin, weighted
% business hours; equals margin_primary on the quality rows of
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.csv
\newcommand{\dgEThreeQualMarginPrimary}{10}
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.md the tighter of the two secondary quality
% margins reported beside the primary one, weighted business hours
\newcommand{\dgEThreeQualMarginTight}{5}
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.md 'Binary outcomes: primary' margin, percentage
% points; equals margin_primary on the binary rows of
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.csv
\newcommand{\dgEThreeBinaryMarginPrimary}{5.0}
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.md the looser of the two secondary binary
% margins reported beside the primary one, percentage points
\newcommand{\dgEThreeBinaryMarginWide}{10.0}
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.csv verdict_margin_low = 'equivalence
% established' over the loose-budget quality_mean_bh rows: arms whose
% end-task quality is equivalent within the tighter quality margin
\newcommand{\dgEThreeQualEquivArms}{6}
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.csv loose-budget quality_mean_bh rows (one per
% arm)
\newcommand{\dgEThreeArmsTotal}{6}
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.csv verdict_margin_mid = 'equivalence
% established' over the loose-budget binary cells (the primary margin)
\newcommand{\dgEThreeBinaryEquivPrimary}{9}
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.csv verdict_margin_high = 'equivalence
% established' over the loose-budget binary cells (the widest reported
% margin)
\newcommand{\dgEThreeBinaryEquivWide}{16}
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.csv loose-budget rows on the three binary
% outcomes (false_block, catch, passthrough): 6 arms x 3 outcomes
\newcommand{\dgEThreeBinaryCells}{18}
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.csv verdict_margin_mid = 'indeterminate' over
% the loose-budget binary cells (the primary margin)
\newcommand{\dgEThreeBinaryIndetPrimary}{9}
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.csv verdict_margin_mid outside {'equivalence
% established', 'indeterminate'} over the loose-budget binary cells: cells
% where a difference wider than the primary margin is affirmed
\newcommand{\dgEThreeBinaryRefutedPrimary}{0}
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.md verdict rule: the interval level, in per
% cent, at which the bootstrap, Newcombe and cluster-bootstrap intervals
% must all lie inside the margin for a cell to count as equivalent (the

% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.csv)
\newcommand{\dgEThreeVerdictLevel}{90}
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.csv n_units on the binary cells: matched pairs
% per cell, the 96 labelled violations or their 96 matched benign twins
\newcommand{\dgEThreeMatchedPairs}{96}
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.csv
% min_onedir_discordant_for_sig_holm96realised: pairs that must be
% discordant, all in one direction, before the exact McNemar test can reach
% significance under the correction the manuscript reports
\newcommand{\dgEThreeMinDiscordant}{12}

\newcommand{\dgEThreeMinDiscordantUncorrected}{6}
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.csv mdes80_holm96realised_bestcase: smallest

% in percentage points, with every discordant pair in one direction (a
% floor, not an estimate)
\newcommand{\dgEThreeDetectableRd}{15.1}
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.csv mdes80_alpha05_bestcase: the same quantity
% with no correction, in percentage points
\newcommand{\dgEThreeDetectableRdUncorrected}{8.1}
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.csv loose-budget rows on the three binary
% outcomes and the mean quality outcome: 6 arms x 4 outcomes
\newcommand{\dgEThreeLooseCells}{24}
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.csv sig_attainable_holm96realised = True over
% those cells: cells whose observed discordance was large enough for a

\newcommand{\dgEThreeCellsCouldDetect}{3}
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.csv sig_attainable_alpha05 = True over those

\newcommand{\dgEThreeCellsCouldDetectUncorrected}{10}
% analysis/DG6_e3_intervals.csv estimate, largest absolute paired risk

\newcommand{\dgEThreeMaxRdLoose}{7.3}

% The guard v0.1 to v0.2 correction, measured on the logs rather than

% DG18: THE AGENT-LAYER TESTS RE-RUN WITH THE INSTANCE AS THE EXCHANGEABLE UNIT
% The declared family of 96 tests behind Section 5.4, re-run with the
% paired sign flipped at the instance level rather than the item level,
% under both readings of violation pass-through
% (analysis/DG18_cluster_tests.csv). Every verdict the manuscript prints
% is unchanged, which is what this group records; the generator asserts it
% rather than the prose claiming it. Only the counts prose needs are
% minted, because a p-value that does not move needs no macro.
% ========================================================================
% analysis/DG18_cluster_tests.csv: tests in the declared agent-layer family,
% one reading
\newcommand{\dgClusterTests}{96}
% analysis/DG18_cluster_tests.csv: readings of violation pass-through the
% family was run under (the disposition reading every printed p-value was
% computed on, and the content rule Table tab:e3-rd uses)
\newcommand{\dgClusterReadings}{2}
% analysis/DG18_cluster_tests.csv rows with cited_in_manuscript=True, one
% reading: tests behind a verdict the manuscript prints. Every one of them
% keeps its verdict under the cluster-aware test, at the uncorrected level
% and after Holm; the generator asserts it.
\newcommand{\dgClusterCitedTests}{30}
% analysis/DG18_cluster_tests.csv rows with verdict_change_holm=True
% [reading e8_disposition]: tests whose Holm-corrected verdict changes.
% Neither is printed as a p-value in the paper; both are the guard's effect
% on violation pass-through at the loose budget, which the manuscript
% reports as a rate change.
\newcommand{\dgClusterHolmFlips}{2}

% [reading content_rule]: the same count under the pass-through content
% rule, and the same two cells
\newcommand{\dgClusterHolmFlipsContent}{2}

% ========================================================================
% DG19: THE CERTIFICATE'S SLACK WHERE THE OPTIMUM IS PROVED
% The certified gap minus the gap to the CP-SAT-proved optimum, on the
% rows of the Tier-1 slice the solver closed at the 5-second budget with a
% positive objective (analysis/DG19_tightness.csv). The excess is the
% bound's slack in the units the tolerance is set in, so it is directly
% comparable with tau = 0.20. Two boundaries come with the number and are
% asserted in the generator: every proof sits in the recorded stratum, the
% solver having closed none of the storm instances at either budget, and
% every row of the slice is one the certificate ACCEPTED, so the slack is
% measured away from the refusal boundary rather than on it.
% ========================================================================
% analysis/DG19_tightness.csv n_rows [budget 5 s / optimal_positive /
% excess]: rows the solver proved optimal with a positive objective, the
% population every number in this group is computed on
\newcommand{\dgTightRows}{108}
% analysis/DG19_tightness.csv n_instances [budget 5 s / optimal_positive /
% excess]: instances those rows sit on
\newcommand{\dgTightInstances}{15}
% analysis/DG19_tightness.csv stat_median [budget 5 s / optimal_positive /
% excess]: median slack of the analytic bound, on the same scale as tau
\newcommand{\dgTightExcessMedian}{0.0004}
% analysis/DG19_tightness.csv stat_max [budget 5 s / optimal_positive /
% excess]: largest slack observed, reported as observed and without an
% interval
\newcommand{\dgTightExcessMax}{0.0012}
% analysis/DG19_tightness.csv rows [block=row / budget 5 s /
% optimal_positive] with gap_certified = 0, as a share of the 108 rows: the
% analytic bound already equals the realized objective, so the certificate
% proves those schedules optimal with no solver involved and there is no
% slack to measure
\newcommand{\dgTightZeroGapShare}{63.9\%}
% analysis/DG19_tightness.csv rows [block=row / budget 5 s /
% optimal_positive] with gap_certified = 0
\newcommand{\dgTightZeroGapRows}{69}
% analysis/DG19_tightness.csv min_true_gap_for_block [budget 5 s /
% optimal_positive / excess]: tau minus the largest measured slack. Slack of
% that size can only carry a proposal across the tolerance if its gap to the
% proved optimum is already at least this large.
\newcommand{\dgTightMinTrueGapForBlock}{0.1988}
% analysis/DG19_tightness.csv n_optimal [coverage / budget 5 s /
% c10_replay_400]: rows of the slice the solver closed, all of them in the
% recorded stratum
\newcommand{\dgTightProvedReplay}{144}
% analysis/DG19_tightness.csv n_optimal [coverage / budget 5 s], summed over
% the two storm strata: none of them closed, which is the coverage boundary
% of this measurement
\newcommand{\dgTightProvedStorm}{0}
